tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Paper is a professional design tool for creating user interfaces. The user is working on a 2D canvas composing designs.
The Paper MCP server gives you tools to be a talented designer for web and mobile apps and websites. You can read designs from the user's file, see what the user is doing, and write HTML back into the design as new nodes.

You MUST load the full guide before other Paper tools: get_guide({ topic: "paper-mcp-instructions" }). Do this once per session; call again if a long thread may have dropped guide text.

- Call get_basic_info when starting on a file to learn artboards and dimensions; use get_selection to see user focus. Omit fileId to use the file the user is looking at, or call list_resources to find another.
- pageId defaults to the page the user is viewing; pass it to work on another page without disrupting them. You can't switch their page.

- When done creating or editing, you MUST call finish_working_on_nodes.
- Never show raw node IDs to the user.
- Export to the user's codebase: use get_jsx, get_computed_styles, get_fill_image, etc. for exact values — never read sizes or colors from screenshots.

    34	  Layer.unwrap(

   138	                                  )
   139	                                ),

   199	                            )

   201	                        )
   202	                      )

     2	import {

     4	  Cause,
     5	  Context,
     6	  Duration,
     7	  Effect,

    11	  Predicate,

    20	import {

    22	  WebsiteBrowserToolRegistrationFailed,

    25	
    26	// A declaration checks the native capability without copying its receiver.
    27	// Browser methods can require the original modelContext object as `this`.
    28	const NativeModelContext = Schema.declare<
    29	  Pick<WebMCP.ModelContext, "registerTool">
    30	>(
    31	  (input): input is Pick<WebMCP.ModelContext, "registerTool"> =>
    32	    Predicate.hasProperty(input, "registerTool") &&
    33	    Predicate.isFunction(input.registerTool)
    34	);
    35	const nativeBrowserContext = (websiteOrigin: DocsWebsiteOrigin) =>
    36	  Effect.sync(() => {
    37	    // SSR has no document. Capability detection is lazy at this native host
    38	    // boundary, so importing the module performs no browser work.
    39	    const documentHost = Option.fromNullishOr(globalThis.document);
    40	    if (Option.isNone(documentHost)) {
    41	      return Option.none<Pick<WebMCP.ModelContext, "registerTool">>();
    42	    }
    43	    const origin = Schema.decodeUnknownOption(DocsWebsiteOrigin)(
    44	      globalThis.location.origin
    45	    );
    46	    return Option.isSome(origin) && origin.value.origin === websiteOrigin.origin
    47	      ? Schema.decodeUnknownOption(NativeModelContext)(
    48	          documentHost.value.modelContext
    49	        )
    50	      : Option.none<Pick<WebMCP.ModelContext, "registerTool">>();
    51	  });

    53	// This is the one private browser protocol adapter. Toolkit owns argument
    54	// decoding and result encoding; the registration Scope owns both native tool
    55	// removal and callback fibres. It creates no browser ManagedRuntime.
    56	export const registerWebsiteBrowserTools = Effect.fnUntraced(function* (
    57	  toolkit: Toolkit.WithHandler<typeof WebsiteBrowserToolkit.tools>,
    58	  websiteOrigin: DocsWebsiteOrigin
    59	) {
    60	  const host = yield* nativeBrowserContext(websiteOrigin);
    61	  if (Option.isNone(host)) {
    62	    return;
    63	  }

    65	    yield* FiberSet.makeRuntimePromise<
    66	      Tool.HandlerServices<
    67	        (typeof WebsiteBrowserToolkit.tools)[keyof typeof WebsiteBrowserToolkit.tools]
    68	      >
    69	    >();
    70	  yield* Effect.forEach(
    71	    Record.toEntries(toolkit.tools),
    72	    ([name, tool]) =>
    73	      Effect.gen(function* () {
    74	        const registration = yield* Effect.acquireRelease(
    75	          Effect.sync(() => new AbortController()),
    76	          (controller) => Effect.sync(() => controller.abort())
    77	        );

    80	        // ingress codec, rather than advertising Unknown as the host contract.

    85	          }
    86	        );

    88	          catch: (cause) => {

    90	              Schema.instanceOf(DOMException)
    91	            )(cause).pipe(
    92	              Option.flatMap((error) =>
    93	                Schema.decodeUnknownOption(
    94	                  WebsiteBrowserToolRegistrationFailed.fields.reason
    95	                )(error.name)

    99	              reason: Option.getOrElse(
   100	                refusal,
   101	                () => "unexpected-host-refusal"
   102	              ),
   103	              tool: tool.name,
   104	            });

   106	          try: (signal) =>
   107	            host.value.registerTool(
   108	              {
   109	                annotations: {
   110	                  consequentialHint: false,
   111	                  readOnlyHint: Context.get(tool.annotations, Tool.Readonly),
   112	                  untrustedContentHint: true,
   113	                },
   114	                description:
   115	                  Tool.getDescription(tool) ??
   116	                  "Use the mounted TaxKit calculator's visible commands.",
   117	                execute: (parameters, options) =>

   119	                    toolkit
   120	                      .handle(name, parameters, undefined, {
   121	                        onExcessProperty: "error",
   122	                      })
   123	                      .pipe(
   124	                        Stream.unwrap,
   125	                        Stream.runLast,
   126	                        Effect.flatMap(Effect.fromOption),
   127	                        Effect.map((result) => result.encodedResult),
   128	                        Effect.catchCause((cause) => {
   129	                          if (Cause.hasInterrupts(cause)) {
   130	                            return Effect.interrupt;
   131	                          }

   134	                            Option.filter(AiError.isAiError),
   135	                            Option.exists((value) =>
   136	                              Match.value(value.reason).pipe(
   137	                                Match.tag(
   138	                                  "ToolParameterValidationError",
   139	                                  () => true
   140	                                ),
   141	                                Match.orElse(() => false)
   142	                              )
   143	                            )
   144	                          );

   146	                            Schema.toCodecJson(WebsiteBrowserToolFailure)
   147	                          )(
   148	                            error.pipe(
   149	                              Option.filter(
   150	                                Schema.is(WebsiteBrowserToolFailure)
   151	                              ),

   157	                                      : "service-unavailable",
   158	                                    retry: validation
   159	                                      ? "check-the-visible-form"
   160	                                      : "try-again-manually",
   161	                                  })
   162	                              )
   163	                            )
   164	                          );
   165	                        }),
   166	                        Effect.scoped
   167	                      ),
   168	                    { signal: options.signal }
   169	                  ),
   170	                inputSchema: {
   171	                  ...input.schema,
   172	                  $defs: input.definitions,
   173	                },
   174	                name: tool.name,
   175	              },
   176	              { signal: AbortSignal.any([registration.signal, signal]) }
   177	            ),
   178	        }).pipe(
   179	          Effect.timeoutOrElse({
   180	            duration: Duration.seconds(2),
   181	            orElse: () =>
   182	              Effect.fail(
   183	                new WebsiteBrowserToolRegistrationFailed({
   184	                  reason: "registration-timeout",
   185	                  tool: tool.name,
   186	                })
   187	              ),
   188	          }),

   190	            Effect.logWarning("A TaxKit browser tool could not register.", {
   191	              reason: error.reason,
   192	              tool: error.tool,
   193	            })
   194	          )
   195	        );
   196	      }),
   197	    { concurrency: Array.length(Record.toEntries(toolkit.tools)) }
   198	  );
   199	});

I've mapped the Website's data loading and API calls below. Several things the brief asks about are absent from `apps/web`: `createIsomorphicFn`, `createLoaderRegistry`, `AtomHttpApi`, `AtomRpc`, `defaultStaleTime`/`staleTime`, `runtime.client`, a browser `ManagedRuntime`, and `build/cloudflare.ts`. `RegistryContext` appears only in tests, and there is no browser-side analytics code (no posthog-js). Paths below are relative to `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/.claude/worktrees/taxkit-native-effect-alchemy-f44f82/apps/web/`.

## 1. Router and runtime setup

- **`src/router.tsx:13-25`**: `getRouter` builds the TanStack router.
  - Its context is `{ loadDocsPage, loadDocsSearch, loadSettings }`, taken from `#/lib/loaders`.
  - Settings: `defaultPreload: "intent"`, `scrollRestoration: true`, and custom `parseSearch`/`stringifySearch` from `docs/search-location.boundary.ts:9-33`, which keeps raw URL pairs instead of the JSON parser.
  - `Register` declares `server: { requestContext: WebsiteServerRenderContext }` (`:26-31`).
- **`src/lib/route-context.ts:7-11`**: the `RouterContext` interface, typed from the three loader functions.
- **`src/routes/__root.tsx`**:
  - The loader (`:161-165`) calls `context.loadSettings({ signal: abortController.signal, submission: serverContext?.submission })`.
  - `RootComponent` decodes `data.settings` with `WebsiteSettingsTransport` (`:49-52`), `data.submission` with `WebsiteSubmissionTransport` (`:53-61`) and `data.catalogue` with `WebsiteCatalogueTransport` (`:62-73`).
  - The Atom registry is created at `:86-92`: `<RegistryProvider key={checked.apiOrigin.href} initialValues={[[publicSettingsAtom, Option.some(checked)], [websiteCatalogueAtom, catalogue]]}>`.
  - The checked submission and catalogue reach children through the React contexts `WebsiteSubmissionContext` and `WebsiteCatalogueContext` (`:29-34`).
- **Server runtime, `src/lib/runtime.server.ts:12-23`**: one module-level `ManagedRuntime.make(Layer.mergeAll(...))` per Worker module. It combines:
  - `WebsiteServerLive(env.TAXKIT_API)` with `ConfigProvider.fromUnknown(env)`
  - `CalculatorHostTelemetryLive("website")`
  - `WebsiteAnalyticsRelayLive` on `FetchHttpClient.layer`
  
  `env` comes from `import { env } from "cloudflare:workers"` (`:3`), the only `cloudflare:workers` import in `src`.
- **Browser runtime, `src/lib/calculator.atoms.ts`**: there is no `ManagedRuntime`. The comment at `:37-38` says the React registry owns client acquisition.
  - `publicSettingsAtom` and `websiteCatalogueAtom` are `Atom.make(Option.none()).pipe(Atom.keepAlive)` (`:41-46`).
  - `calculatorRuntime = Atom.runtime((get) => ...)` (`:47-67`). If settings are missing it fails with `TaxKitWebConfigError` (runtime `"client"`). Otherwise it builds `TaxKitRpcClientLive(settings.apiOrigin)` on `BrowserCalculatorPolicyLive` and `FetchHttpClient.layer`.
  - `BrowserCalculatorPolicyLive` (`calculator-policy.browser.layer.ts:14-36`) sets `CollectionPolicyHeader` from `navigator.doNotTrack` on each request: `"1"` means deny, an unknown value or error also means deny.
- **RPC transport**: both RPC clients POST to `new URL("/rpc", origin)` through `RpcClient.makeProtocolHttp` (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:218-223`; `content.live.layer.ts:156-161`).

## 2. Route loaders and data fetching

**`createServerFn` usage** (all in `src/lib/loaders.ts`, all `GET` with no input validator):

| Name | Line | Handler | Exported URL constant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `websiteSettings` | `:13` | `loadWebsiteSettingsServer()` | `WebsiteSettingsFunctionPath = websiteSettings.url` (`:17`) |
| `websiteDocsPage` | `:18` | `loadWebsiteDocsPageServer()` | `WebsiteDocsPageFunctionPath` (`:21`) |
| `websiteDocsSearch` | `:37` | `loadWebsiteDocsSearchServer()` | `WebsiteDocsSearchFunctionPath` (`:40`) |

**Client wrappers.** Each is a small `Effect.runPromise(..., { signal })`.
- `loadWebsiteDocsPage` (`:23-35`) sends `headers: { "x-taxkit-docs-page": path }`.
- `loadWebsiteDocsSearch` (`:41-65`) URI-encodes the term with `WebsiteDocsSearchHeader` into `x-taxkit-docs-search`. A `DocsSearchInputError` is encoded locally as a failed transport `Result`.
- `loadWebsiteSettings` (`:69-82`) maps the result to `{ catalogue, settings, submission }`.

These two `x-taxkit-*` headers are the only loader request headers.

**Path allowlist.** It is built from the generated identities, not mirrored IDs. `src/server.ts:134-165`:
- Any `/_serverFn/*` path other than the three `.url` values gets a 404.
- A method other than GET gets a 405 with `allow: GET`.
- Any query string, any `content-type` header, or an invalid `x-taxkit-docs-search` / `x-taxkit-docs-page` header gets a 400.
- The base is `WebsiteServerFunctionBase = "/_serverFn"` (`src/lib/config.ts:4`), wired in through `vite.config.ts:56`.

**Server handlers** (`src/lib/loaders.server.ts`, marked `server-only`):
- `loadWebsiteSettingsServer` (`:23-54`): runs `application.settings` and `application.catalogue`, each through `Effect.result`, then encodes with `WebsiteSettingsTransport` / `WebsiteCatalogueTransport`. Unexpected causes go to `HttpServerError.causeResponse` and `ErrorReporter.report`, and an empty web Response is returned.
- `loadWebsiteDocsPageServer` (`:56-111`):
  - The path comes from the URL during SSR, or from `x-taxkit-docs-page` only on a `/_serverFn/` call.
  - It is decoded with `DocsPublicPagePath`, then loads settings, `docsNavigation`, `docsPage` and `preloadDocsPresentation`.
  - `DocsPageUnavailable` becomes a `notFound()` die, which passes through. Everything else is encoded as `WebsiteDocsPageTransport`.
- `loadWebsiteDocsSearchServer` (`:113-156`): the term comes from the header or from `WebsiteDocsSearchLocation(url.search)`. It returns `{navigation, results, settings, term}`, encoded as `WebsiteDocsSearchTransport`.

**Envelopes** (`src/lib/schemas.ts`). Each is `Schema.toCodecJson(Schema.Result(success, errorUnion))`:
- `WebsiteSettingsTransport` (`:48`)
- `WebsiteCatalogueTransport` (`:51`)
- `WebsiteDocsPageTransport` (`:62`)
- `WebsiteDocsSearchTransport` (`:123`)
- `WebsiteSubmissionTransport` (`:170`)

`WebsiteServerRenderContext.submission` is at `:183`. Routes restore the envelopes through `docs/route-boundary.ts:11-24`, which maps a decode failure to `DocsRouteTransportError`.

**Routes:**
- **`/`** (`routes/index.tsx`): no loader. Reads `WebsiteSubmissionContext` and renders `TakeHomeCalculator`.
- **`/calculators/$calculatorId`** (`routes/calculators.$calculatorId.tsx:55-91`): no loader. Finds the calculator in `WebsiteCatalogueContext`, redirects `au.pay.take-home` to `/`, and uses `remountDeps` on `calculatorId`.
- **`/agents`**: no loader. Reads `useAtomValue(publicSettingsAtom)` (`:9`).
- **`/search`** (`routes/search.tsx:72-86`): loader `context.loadDocsSearch({ query: readDocsSearchLocation(location.searchStr), ... })`, with `pendingMs: 150` and `shouldReload: true`.
- **`/$`** (`routes/$.tsx:53-57`): loader `context.loadDocsPage({ path: `/${params._splat}` })`, with `pendingMs: 150` and a `notFoundComponent`.

**`websiteCatalogueAtom` consumers.** It is seeded in `__root.tsx:90` and read only in `browser-tools.atoms.ts:150` (`taxkit_find_calculators`). Route components read the catalogue from `WebsiteCatalogueContext` instead.

## 3. Server-side calls to the API

- **`src/lib/config.server.ts`**:
  - `PrivateApiBinding` (`:11-21`) is a `Schema.declare` check that the binding has callable `fetch`, `connect` and `calculatorRequest`. It keeps the original Fetcher object rather than copying its methods.
  - `TaxKitWebServerConfig` (`:22-53`) reads `API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE` (default `"edge"`) and `WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`. Any failure becomes `TaxKitWebConfigError` with runtime `"server"`.
- **`src/lib/live.server.layer.ts`**, `WebsiteServerLive(binding)`:
  - **`localKey` (`:38-48`)**: a rate key fixed to `127.0.0.1`. It is used only when the host mode is `local-emulator` and the API origin is http on `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`.
  - **Calculator transport (`:53-116`)**: with no `CalculatorRequestRateKey`, it calls `fromCloudflareFetcher(binding).fetch`. With a key, it calls `toRpcAsync<typeof TaxKitApiWorker>(binding).calculatorRequest(incoming, NetAddress.formatIp(key))`. The comment at `:60-62` says the native RPC cannot carry an AbortSignal, so cancelling the call does not stop remote work.

## 4. Calculation flow

**Browser (`calculator.atoms.ts:70-231`).** `calculatorPageAtoms = Atom.family(calculatorId => ...)`:
- `calculation = calculatorRuntime.fn<CalculatorRunServiceRequest>()(req => TaxKitRpcClient.calculate(req))` (`:85-90`).
- `submit` (`:114-148`) builds the request with `takeHomeRequestFromForm` / `annualTaxRequestFromForm`. Invalid input sets `formError` and sends `Atom.Interrupt`. Valid input sets `attempt` and the `calculation`.
- `edit` (`:106-113`) and `cancel` (`:101-105`) set `attempt` to none and send `Atom.Interrupt` to `calculation`.
- `view` (`:168-227`, keepAlive) derives `{busy, form, message, report, stale}`, falling back to `savedReport` / `savedMessage`. Errors are mapped through `calculationFailureMessage` (`calculation-failure.ts:9-29`), which shows safe tagged messages and a generic fallback.
- Legacy home aliases are at `:235-251`.

**Containers.** `take-home.container.tsx` and `calculator-page.container.tsx`:
- Seed the server submission with `useAtomInitialValues` (`take-home:44-69`, `calculator-page:47-59`).
- On unmount, interrupt the calculation (`take-home:80-83`, `calculator-page:68-72`) and the browser tools (`:71-74` / `:61-64`).
- The views render `<form action="/" method="post">` (`take-home.view.tsx:28-34`) or `action={`/calculators/${calculatorId}`}` (`calculator-page.view.tsx:43-49`). With JavaScript, `onSubmit` calls `preventDefault()` and then `onCalculate()`.
- The button shows "Calculating…" and is disabled while busy. Messages render with `role="alert"`. The result views use `aria-live="polite"` and show a stale notice (`take-home-result.view.tsx:20-22`, `calculator-page-result.view.tsx:36-38`).

**No-JavaScript POST (`src/server.ts:124-133, 167-261`).**
1. Only POSTs to `/`, `/calculators/au.income-tax.annual` and `/calculators/au.pay.withholdings` are handled. Other POSTs get a 404 (`markdown.response.server.ts:28-30`).
2. The handler is wrapped in `withCalculatorRequestBodyLimit(..., CalculatorRequestBodyPolicy.make({ responseFormat: "html" }))`.
3. It reads `formData()` and decodes `AnnualTaxForm` or `TakeHomeForm`; failures are `WebsiteInputError` → 400.
4. It calls `application.calculate` under `Effect.result` and encodes a `WebsiteSubmission`.
5. It re-renders as a synthetic GET with `content-length` and `content-type` removed, passing `{ context: { submission } }`. The root loader then forwards `serverContext.submission`.

**Body limit** (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts`):
- `CalculatorRequestBodyLimit = ByteSize.kibibytes(64)` (`:33`) and `CalculatorRequestBodyDeadline = Duration.seconds(5)` (`:34`).
- The stream is counted chunk by chunk with a timeout, plus a monotonic-clock re-check for late synchronous reads (`:50-83`).
- Failures return 413 (size) or 408 (deadline) as a fixed HTML page (`:84-102`).

**Cancellation:**
- The request signal is passed to `appRuntime.runPromise` (`server.ts:283`) and to the server-function runners.
- Browser: `Atom.Interrupt` on edit, cancel or unmount.
- The binding RPC path cannot carry an abort signal (`live.server.layer.ts:60-62`).

## 6. WebMCP, browser tools and analytics

- **`browser-tools.toolkit.ts:16-62`**: five tools: `taxkit_find_calculators`, `taxkit_read_calculator`, `taxkit_fill_calculator`, `taxkit_calculate_visible_form`, `taxkit_read_result`.
- **`browser-tools.atoms.ts:20-185`**: `browserCalculatorToolsAtom = Atom.family(id => calculatorRuntime.fn<"register">()(...))`.
  - Calculate uses the page's `submit` and waits on `AtomRegistry.getResult`, raced against an attempt change, with a 12 s timeout and cleanup through `page.cancel`.
  - Registration is held open with `Effect.never` until React interrupts it.
- **`browser-tools.boundary.ts`**:
  - `nativeBrowserContext` (`:35-51`) registers only if a `document` exists, `location.origin` equals `websiteOrigin.origin`, and `document.modelContext.registerTool` exists.
  - `registerWebsiteBrowserTools` (`:56-199`) uses `FiberSet.makeRuntimePromise`, an `AbortController` per tool, and a 2 s registration timeout. Failures are logged as a warning.
- **Analytics.** There is no client SDK in `src`. The server relay works as follows:
  - Requests to `/ingest/*` go to `server.ts:61-87`, then `WebsiteAnalyticsRelay`.
  - `relay.adapter.layer.ts` accepts POST only, at the exact path `/ingest/e/`.
  - The `Origin` header and the request URL origin must both equal `WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` (`:87-116`), otherwise 403.
  - The media type must be JSON or text/plain, and the query may contain only `retry_count` (`schemas.ts`).
  - A denied collection policy returns 204. Request and response bodies are capped at 65,536 bytes (`schemas.ts:4`).
  - It forwards to `https://us.i.posthog.com/e/` (`:175`) with `redirect: "manual"` and `credentials: "omit"`, under a 5 s deadline (`:272-283`).
  - Failure status codes are mapped at `server.ts:69-82`.
